title: BSE Gains as CEO Says NSE Cannot List on Own Platform, Setting Up India's Biggest IPO Battle
excerpt: BSE CEO Sundararaman Ramamurthy's declaration that NSE must list on a rival exchange positions BSE as the sole venue for what could be India's largest-ever IPO.
body:
• BSE CEO Sundararaman Ramamurthy stated that NSE cannot list its shares on its own platform under current regulations
  • NSE's upcoming IPO, expected in the second half of September, will be structured as a pure Offer for Sale by existing shareholders
  • Bloomberg reported NSE is exploring a "permitted to trade" framework to allow its shares to trade on its own platform after listing on BSE
  • The NSE IPO could be valued at around Rs 7 trillion, making it one of India's largest public offerings ever

BSE shares gained on Thursday after CEO Sundararaman Ramamurthy declared that the National Stock Exchange cannot list its shares on its own platform under India's existing regulatory framework — a statement that positions BSE as the sole listing venue for what is shaping up to be one of India's largest-ever initial public offerings.

The NSE is preparing for a much-anticipated IPO, reportedly targeting the second half of September, subject to SEBI approval of its draft prospectus. NSE CEO Ashish Chauhan has said the offering will be structured entirely as an Offer for Sale, with existing shareholders selling their stakes rather than the exchange raising fresh capital.

The Self-Listing Dilemma

Indian regulations prohibit a stock exchange from listing on its own platform. This means NSE's shares must be formally listed on BSE, Asia's oldest exchange. NSE currently has nearly 195,000 shareholders who collectively own 100% of the exchange, and a 4-4.5% stake sale has been discussed.

"NSE currently has nearly 195,000 shareholders who collectively own 100% of the exchange, and a 4-4.5% stake sale has been discussed."

However, Bloomberg reported last month that NSE is exploring whether its shares could trade on its own platform under the "permitted to trade" category — a framework that allows securities to trade on NSE without being formally listed there. Around 250 companies, including Elantas Beck India and Goodyear India, already trade on NSE under this arrangement.

Any such move would require SEBI approval, and discussions are ongoing. In 2019, NSE revised its index eligibility rules to allow securities under the permitted-to-trade framework to qualify for Nifty index inclusion — a change that could eventually make NSE's own shares eligible for its benchmark indices.

What It Means for BSE

For BSE, the NSE IPO represents a significant revenue opportunity. All trading volumes generated on NSE's counter by investors and traders would add to BSE's transaction income. Rajesh Palviya of Axis Securities told Livemint that the listing could create broader thematic value for the exchange sector, benefiting BSE as funds increase exposure to exchanges.

The flipside emerged when Bloomberg's report about NSE's self-trading plans briefly sent BSE shares down 2% on August 20, as investors worried about potential volume migration. BSE had earlier risen on news of its MSCI-linked derivatives agreement, which would see the exchange explore futures and options contracts linked to MSCI indices.

IPO Timeline and Valuation

SEBI Chief Tuhin Kanta Pandey had indicated the exchange could receive IPO approval by end of August, with the filing involving a draft prospectus review. Analysts have pegged NSE's potential valuation at approximately Rs 7 trillion, a premium to its current estimated valuation of around Rs 5.07 trillion.

NSE's dominance in India's equity derivatives market makes its IPO closely watched by both retail and institutional investors. Retail investors' shareholding in the exchange rose to 12.12% in Q3 FY26 from 9.89% the prior quarter.

Looking Ahead

The regulatory resolution of whether NSE shares can eventually trade on both exchanges will shape how investors access the stock post-listing. For now, BSE stands as the guaranteed beneficiary of whatever trading activity NSE's public debut generates.
